01
Before the first verse · Vol. 3, p. 174

Opening of the surah

Vol. 3, p. 174
Sūrat al-Muʾminūn (Meccan; it has one hundred and nineteen verses, and one hundred and eighteen according to the Kūfans) [revealed after Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ]. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
سورة المؤمنون مكية، وهي مائة وتسع عشرة آية. وثماني عشرة عند الكوفيين [نزلت بعد سورة الأنبياء] بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 174
1. (1). "Had the physicians been around me, / and had the healers been with the physicians." The original is "kānū ḥawlī"; he shortened it, and shortened "al-aṭibbāʾ" by metrical necessity; they are the scholars of medicine. Al-asāt: plural of āsin, like al-suʿāt, plural of sāʿin; they are those among the physicians who undertake the treatment, from al-asā, like al-fatā, meaning treatment. Al-isāʾ (with kasra): medicine, and perhaps it is the original form of the report, as shifāʾ is reported; so its proper place is under the letter alif.
2. . Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "There is disagreement about faith on two views: the first, that everyone who utters the two testimonies with his heart agreeing with his tongue has been described by faith; the other, that it is a descriptor of praise that only the pious and righteous deserve, not the sinful and wretched." Aḥmad said: The first is the school of the Ashʿarites, and the second is the school of the Muʿtazila. The sinful monotheist is, according to them, neither a believer nor a disbeliever. Had the Muʿtazila not built upon this belief the prohibition of Paradise to the sinful monotheist, on the ground that he does not fall under the promise to the believers, the discussion with them would be merely verbal; but they built upon it a grave matter of the fundamentals and principles of religion. The Qāḍī transmitted from them in his epistle on faith a long confusion: he transmitted from their early authorities such as ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd and his generation that faith is affirmation with the heart together with all the obligations of religion, in doing and in leaving. And he transmitted from Abū al-Hudhayl al-ʿAllāf that faith is all the obligations of religion and its supererogatory acts. The summary of the Qāḍī's proof for the Sunnīs is that faith in language is bare affirmation, by agreement, so it must be the same in the sharīʿa, acting on His saying "And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people," together with its freedom from contradiction by transmitted reports, since if there had been another meaning for his Prophet ﷺ and he had explained it, it would have been transmitted, because it is among the things on which the principle of promise and threat is built, and it was not transmitted, because transmission is either solitary (āḥād) or mass-transmitted (tawātur), to the end of its material.
1. (1) . فلو أن الأطباء كان حولي
…. وكان مع الأطباء الأساة الأصل: كانوا حولي، فقصره وقصر «الأطباء» لضرورة الوزن وهم علماء الطب. والأساة: جمع آس، كالسعاة: جمع ساع، وهم المباشرون للعلاج من الأطباء، من الأسى كالفتى، بمعنى المداواة. والاساء- بالكسر-: الدواء، ولعله أصل الرواية، كما روى الشفاء، فحقه حرف الألف.
2. . قال محمود: «اختلف في الايمان على قولين، أحدهما: أن كل من نطق بالشهادتين مواطئا قلبه لسانه فقد اتصف بالايمان. والآخر: أنه صفة مدح لا يستحقها الا البر التقى دون الفاسق الشقي» قال أحمد: والأول مذهب الأشعرية، والثاني مذهب المعتزلة. والموحد الفاسق عندهم لا مؤمن ولا كافر. ولو لم يبن المعتزلة على هذا المعتقد تحريم الجنة على الموحد الفاسق بناء على أنه لا يندرج في وعد المؤمنين، لكان البحث معهم لفظيا، ولكن رتبوا على ذلك أمرا عظيما من أصول الدين وقواعده. وقد نقل القاضي عنهم في رسالة الايمان خبطا طويلا، فنقل عن قدمائهم كعمرو بن عبيد وطبقته أن الايمان هو التصديق بالقلب وجميع فرائض الدين فعلا وتركا. ونقل عن أبى الهذيل العلاف أن الايمان هو جميع فرائض الدين ونوافله. ومختصر دليل القاضي لأهل السنة أن الايمان لغة هو مجرد التصديق اتفاقا، فوجب أن يكون كذلك شرعا، عملا بقوله تعالى وَما أَرْسَلْنا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا بِلِسانِ قَوْمِهِ مع سلامته عن معارضة النقل، فانه لو كان لنبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام ولو بينه لنقل لأنه مما يبتنى عليه قاعدة الوعد والوعيد، ولم ينقل، لأن النقل إما آحاد أو تواتر إلى آخر مادته.
02
Q 23:1–2 · Vol. 3, pp. 174–175

Verses 1 to 2

The verses as the commentary quotes them
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. "Certainly will the believers have succeeded:" (1) "those who during their prayer are humbly submissive," (2)
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ (1) الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ (2)
Vol. 3, p. 174
"Qad" is the opposite of "lammā": it confirms what is expected, while "lammā" negates it, and there is no doubt that the believers were expecting such good news, which is the report of the certainty of success for them, so they were addressed with a particle that indicates the certainty of what they expected. Al-falāḥ: attainment of what is sought; it is also said: remaining in good. "Aflaḥa" means he entered into falāḥ, like absharа, he entered into glad tidings. One says: aflaḥahu, meaning he brought him to falāḥ. On this is the reading of Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif: ufliḥa, in the passive. From him also: aflaḥū, on the construction "the fleas ate me" (akalūnī l-barāghīth), or on indeterminacy followed by explanation. From him also: aflaḥu, with a ḍamma and no wāw, contenting itself with the ḍamma in place of the wāw, as in the verse: "Had the physicians been around me (1)."
قَدْ نقيضة «لما» هي تثبت المتوقع و «لما» تنفيه، ولا شك أن المؤمنين كانوا متوقعين لمثل هذه البشارة وهي الإخبار بثبات الفلاح لهم، فخوطبوا بما دل على ثبات ما توقعوه. والفلاح: الظفر بالمراد. وقيل: البقاء في الخير. وأَفْلَحَ دخل في الفلاح، كأبشر: دخل في البشارة. ويقال: أفلحه: أصاره إلى الفلاح. وعليه قراءة طلحة بن مصرف: أفلح، على البناء للمفعول. وعنه: أفلحوا، على: أكلونى البراغيث. أو على الإبهام والتفسير. وعنه: أفلح، بضمة بغير واو، اجتزاء بها عنها، كقوله: فلو أنّ الاطبّا كان حولي «1»
Question
If you ask: what is the believer?
فإن قلت: ما المؤمن؟
Answer
I say: in language he is the one who affirms [something as true]. As for the sharīʿa, there is disagreement about it on two views: the first, that everyone who utters the two testimonies, with his heart agreeing with his tongue, is a believer; the other, that it is a descriptor of praise that only the pious and righteous deserve, not the sinful and wretched (2)
قلت: هو في اللغة المصدق. وأما في الشريعة فقد اختلف فيه على قولين، أحدهما: أنّ كل من نطق بالشهادتين مواطئا قلبه لسانه فهو مؤمن. والآخر أنه صفة مدح لا يستحقها إلا البرّ التقىّ دون الفاسق الشقىّ «2»
Vol. 3, p. 175
Humility (khushūʿ) in prayer is fear of the heart and keeping the gaze fixed (ilbād al-baṣar); on the authority of Qatāda: it is keeping it on the place of prostration. On the authority of the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to pray with his sight raised to the sky, and when this verse was revealed he cast his sight toward his place of prostration (1); and when one of the scholars stood to pray, he held the Most Merciful in awe lest he fix his gaze on anything, or speak to himself about any worldly affair. It is also said: it is gathering one's concern for it and turning away from everything else. Part of khushūʿ is that one observes the proper manners, so he guards against gathering up the sleeve of the garment, fiddling with his body and clothes, turning around, stretching, yawning, shutting the eyes, covering the mouth, letting the garment hang loose (sadl), cracking the fingers, interlacing the fingers, resting the hands on the hips (ikhtiṣār), and turning over pebbles. It is reported on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ that he saw a man fiddling with his beard in prayer and said: "If his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble (2)." Al-Ḥasan looked at a man who was playing with pebbles while saying "O God, marry me to the ḥūr al-ʿīn," and said: "What a wretched suitor you are! You propose marriage while you play."
الخشوع في الصلاة: خشية القلب وإلباد البصر- عن قتادة: وهو إلزامه موضع السجود. وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه كان يصلى رافعا بصره إلى السماء، فلما نزلت هذه الآية رمى ببصره نحو مسجده «1» ، وكان الرجل من العلماء إذا قام إلى الصلاة هاب الرحمن أن يشدّ بصره إلى شيء، أو يحدّث نفسه بشأن من شأن الدنيا. وقيل: هو جمع الهمة لها، والإعراض عما سواها. ومن الخشوع: أن يستعمل الآداب، فيتوقى كفّ الثوب، والعبث بجسده وثيابه، والالتفات، والتمطي، والتثاؤب، والتغميض، وتغطية الفم، والسدل، والفرقعة، والتشبيك، والاختصار، وتقليب الحصا. روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أبصر رجلا يعبث بلحيته في الصلاة فقال «لو خشع قلبه خشعت جوارحه «2» » ونظر الحسن إلى رجل يعبث بالحصا وهو يقول: اللهمّ زوجني الحور العين، فقال: بئس الخاطب أنت! تخطب وأنت تعبث.
Question
If you ask: why is prayer annexed to them?
فإن قلت: لم أضيفت الصلاة إليهم؟
Answer
I say: because prayer revolves between the one praying and the one prayed to, and the one praying is the sole beneficiary of it, and it is his provision and store, so it is his prayer; as for the one prayed to, He is rich, exalted above any need of it or benefit from it.
قلت: لأنّ الصلاة دائرة بين المصلى والمصلى له، فالمصلى هو المنتفع بها وحده وهي عدّته وذخيرته فهي صلاته: وأمّا المصلى له، فغنىّ متعال عن الحاجة إليها والانتفاع بها.

1. (1). Al-Ḥākim transmitted it from the narration of Ibn Sīrīn from Abū Hurayra, but he said "so he lowered his head," and said: sound, except that it has been narrated as mursal. The mursal version was transmitted by Abū Dāwūd and al-Ṭabarī from Ibn Sīrīn from the Prophet ﷺ and he said: there is something to consider in it, thus. Al-Wāḥidī transmitted it in al-Asbāb by way of Ibn ʿUlayya, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, as a connected (mawṣūl) report. [.....]
2. . Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī transmitted it in al-Nawādir, in the one hundred and forty-sixth [item], from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra, and in its chain is Sulaymān b. ʿAmr, who is Abū Dāwūd al-Nakhaʿī, one of those accused of fabricating ḥadīth. And in the commentary on al-Bukhārī by Zayn al-Dīn Ibn al-Munayyir, on the authority of the Prophet ﷺ that he said to ʿĀʾisha: "If the heart of this one were humble, his limbs would be humble."
1. (1) . أخرجه الحاكم من رواية ابن سيرين عن أبى هريرة، لكن قال «فطأطأ رأسه وقال صحيح، إلا أنه روى مرسلا اه والمرسل أخرجه أبو داود والطبري عن ابن سيرين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال: فيه نظر هكذا، وأخرجه الواحدي في الأسباب من طريق ابن علية، عن أيوب. عن ابن سيرين موصولا. [.....]
2. . أخرجه الحكيم الترمذي في النوادر في السادس والأربعين بعد المائة من حديث أبى هريرة وفيه سليمان ابن عمرو وهو أبو داود والنخعي أحد من اتهم بوضع الحديث وفي شرح البخاري لزين الدين ابن المنير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال لعائشة «لو خشع قلب هذا لخشعت جوارحه» .
03
Q 23:3 · Vol. 3, pp. 175–176

Verse 3

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And they who turn away from ill speech" (3)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ (3)
Vol. 3, p. 175
Laghw: whatever does not concern you of speech or action, such as play and jesting and whatever manliness requires be discarded and cast aside, meaning that they have enough earnestness to occupy them away from jesting. When He described them with humility in prayer, He followed it with the description of turning away from laghw, so as to join for them the act and the abstention, both of which are burdensome on the souls and which are the two foundations on which religious obligation is built.
اللغو: ما لا يعنيك من قول أو فعل، كاللعب والهزل وما توجب المروءة إلغاءه وإطراحه، يعنى أنّ بهم من الجدّ ما يشغلهم عن الهزل. لما وصفهم بالخشوع في الصلاة، أتبعه الوصف بالإعراض عن اللغو، ليجمع لهم الفعل والترك الشاقين على الأنفس اللذين هما قاعدتا بناء التكليف.
Vol. 3, p. 176

Vol. 3, p. 176
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "Zakāh is applied to mean the entity that is drawn out, and is applied to mean the act of the giver, which is tazkiya; here it is necessary that tazkiya be meant, because of His saying 'fāʿilūn,' since the entity that is drawn out is not something the giver has done. Then he fixed the verbal noun absolutely as that of which it is true that it is an act of the doer; on this basis the entity that is drawn out is a verbal noun in relation to God, Exalted, and likewise the heavens and the earth and every created thing, of substance and accident. He said: so for all events, if it is asked who is their doer, it is said: God or some of the creatures." Aḥmad said: The Sunnī says: the doer of all of them is God alone, who has no partner; but if he is asked with a form derived from the verb on the pattern of the active participle, for example if it is said to him "who is the one standing? who is the one sitting?", he answers with the one at whose hands God created the act, and whom He made its locus, such as Zayd and ʿAmr.
2. . By Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt. Al-azm: drought. Al-azma: the severe, droughty [year]. Al-zakawāt: plural of zakāh, which is applied to the amount drawn from wealth and to the act of drawing it out; so the meaning on the first is: those who pay the zakawāt; and on the second: the doers of that drawing out; and the first is the more apt, because a verbal noun is pluralized only by interpreting it as kinds or instances.
1. (1) . قال محمود: «الزكاة تطلق ويراد بها العين المخرجة، وتطلق ويراد بها فعل المزكى الذي هو التزكية ويتعين هاهنا أن يكون المراد التزكية لقوله فاعِلُونَ إذ العين المخرجة لم يفعلها المزكى، ثم ضبط المصدر على الإطلاق بأنه الذي يصدق عليه أنه فعل الفاعل فعلى هذا تكون العين المخرجة مصدرا بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى، وكذلك السماوات والأرض وكل مخلوق من جوهر وعرض، قال: فجميع الحوادث إذا قيل من فاعلها؟ فيقال: الله أو بعض الخلق» قال أحمد: ويقول السنى: فاعل جميعها هو الله وحده لا شريك له، ولكن إذا سئل بصيغة مشتقة من الفعل على طريقة اسم الفاعل، مثل أن يقال له: من القائم؟ من القاعد؟ أجاب بمن خلق الله الفعل على يديه، وجعله محلا له، كزيد وعمرو.
2. . لأمية بن أبى الصلت. والأزم: الجدب. والأزمة: الشديدة المجدبة. والزكوات: جمع زكاة، تطلق على القدر المخرج من المال وعلى الإخراج، فالمعنى على الأول: المؤدون للزكوات. وعلى الثاني: الفاعلون لذلك الإخراج، والأول أوجه، لأن المصدر لا يجمع إلا بتأويل الأنواع أو المرات.
04
Q 23:4 · Vol. 3, p. 176

Verse 4

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And they who are observers of zakāh" (4)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكاةِ فاعِلُونَ (4)
Vol. 3, p. 176
Zakāh is a noun shared between an entity (ʿayn) and a meaning (maʿnā): the entity is the amount that the one giving zakāh sets apart from the taxable property (niṣāb) for the poor person; and the meaning is the act of the giver, which is tazkiya, and this is what God intended, so He made the givers of zakāh the doers [fāʿilūn] of it, and nothing else is allowable here, because there is no verbal noun (maṣdar) whose meaning is not expressed by the verb, and the one who brings it about is called its doer: you say of the striker "the doer of the striking," of the killer "the doer of the killing," and of the giver of zakāh "the doer of the tazkiya." And on all of this discourse, the verification of it is that you say about all events: who is the doer of this? and you are told: its doer is God or some of the creatures (1). Zakāh, in its sense of the entity, was not barred from having doers attached to it because it falls outside what a doer can take up, but because the creatures are not its doers. A verse of Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt has been recited: "Those who feed food in the year of dearth, and the doers of the zakawāt (2)." It is also possible that by zakāh the entity is meant and an omitted annexed term is supplied, namely "payment" (adāʾ), and taking the verse in this way is sounder, because in it the word is in the plural.
الزكاة اسم مشترك بين عين ومعنى، فالعين: القدر الذي يخرجه المزكى من النصاب إلى الفقير والمعنى: فعل المزكى الذي هو التزكية، وهو الذي أراده الله، فجعل المزكين فاعلين له ولا يسوغ فيه غيره، لأنه ما من مصدر إلا يعبر عن معناه بالفعل ويقال لمحدثه فاعل، تقول للضارب: فاعل الضرب، وللقاتل: فاعل القتل: وللمزكى: فاعل التزكية. وعلى هذا الكلام كله والتحقيق فيه أنك تقول في جميع الحوادث: من فاعل هذا؟ فيقال لك: فاعله الله أو بعض الخلق «1» . ولم يمتنع الزكاة الدالة على العين أن يتعلق بها فاعلون، لخروجها من صحة أن يتناولها الفاعل، ولكن لأنّ الخلق ليسوا بفاعليها. وقد أنشد لأمية ابن أبى الصلت: المطعمون الطّعام في السّنة الأزمة والفاعلون للزّكوات «2» ويجوز أن يراد بالزكاة: العين، ويقدّر مضاف محذوف وهو الأداء، وحمل البيت على هذا أصحّ، لأنها فيه مجموعة.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 176
1. (1). Maḥmūd [al-Zamakhsharī] said: "Zakāh is applied to mean the entity that is drawn out, and is applied to mean the act of the giver, which is tazkiya; here it is necessary that tazkiya be meant, because of His saying 'fāʿilūn,' since the entity that is drawn out is not something the giver has done. Then he fixed the verbal noun absolutely as that of which it is true that it is an act of the doer; on this basis the entity that is drawn out is a verbal noun in relation to God, Exalted, and likewise the heavens and the earth and every created thing, of substance and accident. He said: so for all events, if it is asked who is their doer, it is said: God or some of the creatures." Aḥmad said: The Sunnī says: the doer of all of them is God alone, who has no partner; but if he is asked with a form derived from the verb on the pattern of the active participle, for example if it is said to him "who is the one standing? who is the one sitting?", he answers with the one at whose hands God created the act, and whom He made its locus, such as Zayd and ʿAmr.
2. . By Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt. Al-azm: drought. Al-azma: the severe, droughty [year]. Al-zakawāt: plural of zakāh, which is applied to the amount drawn from wealth and to the act of drawing it out; so the meaning on the first is: those who pay the zakawāt; and on the second: the doers of that drawing out; and the first is the more apt, because a verbal noun is pluralized only by interpreting it as kinds or instances.

2. . لأمية بن أبى الصلت. والأزم: الجدب. والأزمة: الشديدة المجدبة. والزكوات: جمع زكاة، تطلق على القدر المخرج من المال وعلى الإخراج، فالمعنى على الأول: المؤدون للزكوات. وعلى الثاني: الفاعلون لذلك الإخراج، والأول أوجه، لأن المصدر لا يجمع إلا بتأويل الأنواع أو المرات.
05
Q 23:5–7 · Vol. 3, pp. 176–177

Verses 5 to 7

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And they who guard their private parts" (5) "except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed" (6) "but whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors" (7)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حافِظُونَ (5) إِلاَّ عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ أَوْ ما مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ (6) فَمَنِ ابْتَغى وَراءَ ذلِكَ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ العادُونَ (7)
Vol. 3, p. 176
"ʿAlā azwājihim" is in the position of a circumstantial clause, that is, those who resort to their wives, or those who are in charge of them, from your saying "so-and-so was over so-and-so [as husband], then he died and left her, and another succeeded over her." A parallel: "Ziyād was over al-Baṣra," that is: governor over it. From it is their saying "so-and-so [fem.] is under so-and-so," and from there the woman is called a "bed" (firāsh). The meaning: they are guardians of their private parts
عَلى أَزْواجِهِمْ في موضع الحال، أى الأوّالين على أزواجهم. أو قوّامين عليهنّ، من قولك: كان فلان على فلانة فمات عنها فخلّف عليها فلان. ونظيره: كان زياد على البصرة، أى: واليا عليها. ومنه قولهم: فلانة تحت فلان. ومن ثمة سميت المرأة فراشا. والمعنى: أنهم لفروجهم
Vol. 3, p. 177
guardians in all circumstances, except in the state of their marrying or taking concubines; or "ʿalā" is attached to an omitted word that "ghayr malūmīn" indicates, as though it were said: "they are blamed except concerning their wives," that is: they are blamed for every sexual contact except what has been permitted to them, for in that they are not blamed. Or you make it connected to "ḥāfiẓīn," from your saying "iḥfaẓ ʿalayya ʿinān farasī" [guard for me the rein of my horse], by its including the sense of negation, as there was included in their saying "nashadtuka bi-llāh illā faʿalta" the meaning "I ask nothing of you except your doing [it]."
حافظون في كافة الأحوال، إلا في حال تزوّجهم أو تسريهم، أو تعلق عَلى بمحذوف يدل عليه غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ كأنه قيل: يلامون إلا على أزواجهم، أى: يلامون على كل مباشر إلا على ما أطلق لهم، فإنهم غير ملومين عليه. أو تجعله صلة لحافظين، من قولك: احفظ علىّ عنان فرسي، على تضمينه معنى النفي، كما ضمن قولهم: نشدتك بالله إلا فعلت معنى ما طلبت منك إلا فعلك.
Question
If you ask: why was it not said "man malakat"?
فإن قلت هلا قيل: من ملكت؟
Answer
I say: because what is meant, of the class of rational beings, is what is treated like the non-rational, namely females. He made the exception a limit that necessitates stopping at it, then said: whoever introduces a seeking beyond this limit, despite its breadth and extent, which is the permission of four free women and as many slave women as you wish, "then those are the transgressors," perfect in aggression and utmost in it.
قلت: لأنه أريد من جنس العقلاء ما يجرى مجرى غير العقلاء وهم الإناث جعل المستثنى حدا أوجب الوقوف عنده، ثم قال: فمن أحدث ابتغاء وراء هذا الحدّ مع فسحته واتساعه، وهو إباحة أربع من الحرائر، ومن الإماء ما شئت فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الكاملون في العدوان المتناهون فيه.
Question
If you ask: is there in it proof for the prohibition of temporary marriage (mutʿa)?
فإن قلت: هل فيه دليل على تحريم المتعة؟
Answer
I say: no, because the woman married by a mutʿa marriage is among the wives if the marriage is valid.
قلت: لا، لأنّ المنكوحة نكاح المتعة من جملة الأزواج إذا صحّ النكاح.

Vol. 3, p. 176

Q 23:8 · Vol. 3, p. 177

Verse 8

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And they who are to their trusts and their promises attentive" (8)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَماناتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ راعُونَ (8)
Vol. 3, p. 177
It has also been read: li-amānatihim. The thing entrusted and the thing covenanted are called amāna and ʿahd. From it comes His saying "Indeed, God commands you to render trusts to their owners," and He said "and betray your trusts"; but it is entities that are rendered, not meanings, and it is the thing entrusted that is betrayed, not the trust in itself. Al-rāʿī: the one who stands over something with preservation and improvement, like the shepherd of sheep and the shepherd of subjects. One says: "who is the rāʿī of this thing?" that is, its manager and owner. It may be general, covering everything they were entrusted with and covenanted on, from God, Exalted, and from creatures; or specific, to the trusts and covenants of people that they carry.
وقرئ: لأمانتهم. سمى الشيء المؤتمن عليه والمعاهد عليه أمانة وعهدا. ومنه قوله تعالى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَماناتِ إِلى أَهْلِها وقال وَتَخُونُوا أَماناتِكُمْ وإنما تؤدّى العيون لا المعاني، ويخان المؤتمن عليه، لا الأمانة في نفسها. والراعي: القائم على الشيء بحفظ وإصلاح كراعى الغنم وراعى الرعية. ويقال: من راعى هذا الشيء؟ أى متوليه وصاحبه: ويحتمل العموم في كل ما ائتمنوا عليه وعوهدوا من جهة الله تعالى ومن جهة الخلق، والخصوص فيما حملوه من أمانات الناس وعهودهم.
07
Q 23:9 · Vol. 3, p. 177

Verse 9

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And they who carefully maintain their prayers" (9)
وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلَواتِهِمْ يُحافِظُونَ (9)
Vol. 3, p. 177
It has also been read: ʿalā ṣalātihim [in the singular].
وقرئ عَلى صَلَواتِهِمْ.
Question
If you ask: how is the mention of prayer repeated at the beginning and at the end?
فإن قلت: كيف كرّر ذكر الصلاة أوّلا وآخرا؟
Answer
I say: they are two different mentions, so it is not a repetition. They were described first by humility in their prayer and last by maintaining it. This is that they do not forget it, perform it at its times, establish its pillars, and appoint their souls over it with concern for it and for what must complete its attributes. Moreover, it was singular first to convey humility in the genus of prayer, whichever prayer it be, and plural last to convey maintaining its number: namely the five prayers, the witr, the sunan arranged with each prayer, the Friday prayer, the two ʿīd prayers, the funeral prayer, the prayer for rain, the prayer of the eclipses of sun and moon, the ḍuḥā prayer, the night vigil, the tasbīḥ prayer, the prayer of need, and other supererogatory prayers.
قلت: هما ذكران مختلفان فليس بتكرير. وصفوا أوّلا بالخشوع في صلاتهم، وآخرا بالمحافظة عليها. وذلك أن لا يسهوا عنها، ويؤدّوها في أوقاتها، ويقيموا أركانها، ويوكلوا نفوسهم بالاهتمام بها وبما ينبغي أن تتمّ به أوصافها. وأيضا فقد وحدت أوّلا ليفاد الخشوع في جنس الصلاة أىّ صلاة كانت، وجمعت آخرا لتفاد المحافظة على أعدادها: وهي الصلوات الخمس، والوتر، والسنن المرتبة مع كل صلاة وصلاة الجمعة، والعيدين والجنازة، والاستسقاء، والكسوف والخسوف، وصلاة الضحى، والتهجد وصلاة التسبيح، وصلاة الحاجة، وغيرها من النوافل.
08
Q 23:10–11 · Vol. 3, pp. 177–178

Verses 10 to 11

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Those are the inheritors" (10) "who will inherit al-Firdaws; they will abide therein eternally." (11)
أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْوارِثُونَ (10) الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ (11)
Vol. 3, p. 177
That is: "those" who combine these attributes "are the inheritors," the ones worthy to be called heirs
أى أُولئِكَ الجامعون لهذه الأوصاف هُمُ الْوارِثُونَ الأحقاء بأن يسموا ورّاثا
Vol. 3, p. 178
to the exclusion of all others; then He glossed "the inheritors" with His saying "who will inherit al-Firdaws," bringing a grandeur and eloquence about their inheritance that does not escape the observer. The meaning of inheritance is what was discussed in Sūrat Maryam. He made al-Firdaws feminine on the interpretation of "the Garden"; it is the wide orchard that combines kinds of fruit. It is related that God, Mighty and Majestic, built the Garden of al-Firdaws with one brick of gold and one brick of silver, and put in its interstices fragrant musk (al-misk al-adhfar). In one report: and one brick of scattered musk, and He planted in it the best fruit and the best sweet basil.
دون من عداهم، ثم ترجم الوارثين بقوله الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ فجاء بفخامة وجزالة لإرثهم لا تخفى على الناظر. ومعنى الإرث: ما مرّ في سورة مريم. أنث الفردوس على تأويل الجنة، وهو: البستان الواسع الجامع لأصناف الثمر. روى أنّ الله عز وجل بنى جنة الفردوس لبنة من ذهب ولبنة من فضة، وجعل خلالها المسك الأذفر. وفي رواية: ولبنة من مسك مذرّى وغرس فيها من جيد الفاكهة وجيد الريحان.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 178
1. (1). In the chapter there is also [a report] from Anas, who said: ʿUmar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four [matters]," and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and in it: "so there was revealed: 'And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay,' up to His saying 'another creation.' So I said: 'So blessed is God, the best of creators.' So it was revealed."
1. (1) . وفي الباب عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربى في أربع فذكر الحديث- وفيه: فنزلت وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ، إلى قوله خَلْقاً آخَرَ. فقلت فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخالِقِينَ. فنزلت»
09
Q 23:12–14 · Vol. 3, pp. 178–179

Verses 12 to 14

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay." (12) "Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging." (13) "Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump [of flesh], and We made the lump into bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is God, the best of creators." (14)
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ (12) ثُمَّ جَعَلْناهُ نُطْفَةً فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ (13) ثُمَّ خَلَقْنَا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْعَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنَا الْمُضْغَةَ عِظاماً فَكَسَوْنَا الْعِظامَ لَحْماً ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْناهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخالِقِينَ (14)
Vol. 3, p. 178
Sulāla: the quintessence, because it is drawn (tusall) from among the dregs, and the pattern fuʿāla is a pattern of smallness [of quantity], like qulāma and qumāma. On the authority of al-Ḥasan: water in the midst of clay.
السلالة: الخلاصة، لأنها تسلّ من بين الكدر، و «فعالة» بناء للقلة كالقلامة والقمامة. وعن الحسن: ماء بين ظهراني الطين.
Question
If you ask: what is the difference between the two "min"s?
فإن قلت: ما الفرق بين من ومن؟
Answer
I say: the first is for the starting point and the second for explanation, as in "min al-awthān" [from the idols].
قلت: الأوّل للابتداء، والثاني للبيان، كقوله مِنَ الْأَوْثانِ.
Question
If you ask: what is the meaning of "We made him," man, "a sperm-drop"?
فإن قلت: ما معنى: جَعَلْناهُ الإنسان نطفة؟
Answer
I say: its meaning is that He created the substance of man first as clay, then made his substance after that a sperm-drop. Qarār: the place of settling, and the womb is meant. It was described by "makīn" [firm], which is a description of the one settled in it, as you say "a road that is traveling" [ṭarīq sāʾir]; or by its own firmness, because it was made firm as it is and was secured. It has been read: ʿaẓman fa-kasawnā al-ʿaẓma; ʿiẓāman fa-kasawnā al-ʿiẓāma; ʿaẓman fa-kasawnā al-ʿiẓāma; and ʿiẓāman fa-kasawnā al-ʿaẓma: the singular was put in place of the plural because there is no ambiguity, since man has many bones. "Another creation": that is, a creation distinct from the first creation by a distinction how far! In that He made him an animal when he was inanimate, speaking when he was dumb, hearing when he was deaf, seeing when he was born blind, and placed in his inside and outside, indeed in every organ of his organs and every part of his parts, wonders of nature and marvels of wisdom that cannot be grasped by the description of a describer nor reached by the explanation of an explainer. Abū Ḥanīfa used it as an argument regarding one who usurped an egg that hatched in his possession: he said: he is liable for the egg and does not return the chick, because it is another creation besides the egg. "So blessed is God": exalted is His command in His power and knowledge; "the best of creators": that is, the best of those who determine, in determining; the specifier was left out because "creators" indicates it. Similar is the omission of the one permitted in His saying "Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought," because the relative clause indicates it. It is reported on the authority of ʿUmar ؓ that when the Messenger of God ﷺ reached His saying "another creation," he said: "So blessed is God, the best of creators (1)." It is reported that ʿAbdallāh b. Saʿd b. Abī Sarḥ used to write for the Prophet, may God bless
قلت: معناه أنه خلق جوهر الإنسان أوّلا طينا، ثم جعل جوهره بعد ذلك نطفة. القرار: المستقرّ، والمراد الرحم. وصفت بالمكانة التي هي صفة المستقرّ فيها، كقولك. طريق سائر. أو بمكانتها في نفسها، لأنها مكنت بحيث هي وأحرزت. قرئ: عظما فكسونا العظم. وعظاما فكسونا العظام وعظما فكسونا العظام. وعظاما فكسونا العظم: وضع الواحد مكان الجمع لزوال اللبس، لأنّ الإنسان ذو عظام كثيرة خَلْقاً آخَرَ أى خلقا مباينا للخلق الأوّل مباينة ما أبعدها، حيث جعله حيوانا وكان جمادا، وناطقا وكان أبكم، وسميعا وكان أصم، وبصيرا وكان أكمه، وأودع باطنه وظاهره- بل كل عضو من أعضائه وكل جزء من أجزائه- عجائب فطرة وغرائب حكمة لا تدرك بوصف الواصف ولا تبلغ بشرح الشارح: وقد احتجّ به أبو حنيفة فيمن غصب بيضة فأفرخت عنده قال: يضمن البيضة ولا يرد الفرخ، لأنه خلق آخر سوى البيضة فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ فتعالى أمره في قدرته وعلمه أَحْسَنُ الْخالِقِينَ أى: أحسن المقدّرين تقديرا، فترك ذكر المميز لدلالة الخالقين عليه. ونحوه: طرح المأذون فيه في قوله أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقاتَلُونَ لدلالة الصلة. وروى عن عمر رضى الله عنه أنّ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما بلغ قوله خلقا آخر، قال: فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين «1» . وروى أنّ عبد الله بن سعد بن أبى سرح كان يكتب للنبي صلى الله
Vol. 3, p. 179
him and grant him peace, and he uttered that before it was dictated; so the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Write it thus; it was revealed." ʿAbdallāh said: "If Muḥammad is a prophet to whom revelation comes, then I am a prophet to whom revelation comes," so he joined Mecca as a disbeliever, and then became Muslim on the day of the conquest (1).
عليه وسلم، فنطق بذلك قبل إملائه، فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «اكتب هكذا نزلت» فقال عبد الله: إن كان محمد نبيا يوحى إليه فأنا نبىّ يوحى إلىّ، فلحق بمكة كافرا، ثم أسلم يوم الفتح «1» .
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 178
1. (1). In the chapter there is also [a report] from Anas, who said: ʿUmar said: "I agreed with my Lord in four [matters]," and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and in it: "so there was revealed: 'And certainly did We create man from an extract of clay,' up to His saying 'another creation.' So I said: 'So blessed is God, the best of creators.' So it was revealed."
1. (1) . وفي الباب عن أنس قال: قال عمر: وافقت ربى في أربع فذكر الحديث- وفيه: فنزلت وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنْ سُلالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ، إلى قوله خَلْقاً آخَرَ. فقلت فَتَبارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخالِقِينَ. فنزلت»
Vol. 3, p. 179
1. (1). Thus al-Thaʿlabī mentioned it from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, and al-Wāḥidī ascribed it to al-Kalbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both.
1. (1) . كذا ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وعزاه الواحدي إلى الكلبي. عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما.
10
Q 23:15–16 · Vol. 3, p. 179

Verses 15 to 16

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"Then indeed, you, after that, will die." (15) "Then indeed, you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected." (16)
ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ لَمَيِّتُونَ (15) ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ تُبْعَثُونَ (16)
Vol. 3, p. 179
Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn Muḥayṣin read: la-māʾitūn. The difference between al-mayyit and al-māʾit is that al-mayyit, like al-ḥayy, is a fixed attribute, whereas al-māʾit indicates occurrence [of an event]. You say: Zayd is māʾit now, and māʾit tomorrow, as you say "he will die." Similar are ḍayyiq and ḍāʾiq, in His saying "and your breast is constrained by it." He made causing death, which is the nullification of life, and resurrection, which is the restoration of what He has annihilated and nullified, two further proofs of great power after the bringing into being and the origination.
قرأ ابن أبى عبلة وابن محيصن: لمائتون. والفرق بين الميت والمائت: أنّ الميت كالحي صفة ثابتة. وأمّا المائت، فيدل على الحدوث. تقول: زيد مائت الآن، ومائت غدا، كقولك يموت. ونحوهما: ضيق وضائق، في قوله تعالى وَضائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ جعل الإماتة التي هي إعدام الحياة، والبعث الذي هو إعادة ما يفنيه ويعدمه: دليلين أيضا على اقتدار عظيم بعد الإنشاء والاختراع.
Question
If you ask: then there is no life except the life of bringing into being and the life of resurrection?
فإن قلت: فإذا لا حياة إلا حياة الإنشاء وحياة البعث.
Answer
I say: the mention of the two lives does not negate the third, which is the life of the grave, just as if you mentioned two thirds of what you have and left unmentioned the third, that would be no proof that the third is not with you. Moreover, the aim is to mention these three kinds: bringing into being, causing death, and restoration, and the one left unmentioned belongs to the kind of restoration.
قلت: ليس في ذكر الحياتين نفى الثالثة وهي حياة القبر، كما لو ذكرت ثلثي ما عندك وطويت ذكر ثلثه لم يكن دليلا على أن الثلث ليس عندك. وأيضا فالغرض ذكر هذه الأجناس الثلاثة: الإنشاء والإماتة والإعادة، والمطوى ذكرها من جنس الإعادة.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 179
1. (1). Thus al-Thaʿlabī mentioned it from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, and al-Wāḥidī ascribed it to al-Kalbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both.
1. (1) . كذا ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وعزاه الواحدي إلى الكلبي. عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما.
11
Q 23:17 · Vol. 3, p. 179

Verse 17

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And We have created above you seven pathways, and never have We been unaware of [Our] creation." (17)
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعَ طَرائِقَ وَما كُنَّا عَنِ الْخَلْقِ غافِلِينَ (17)
Vol. 3, p. 179
Al-ṭarāʾiq: the heavens, because they were layered one over another, like the layering of sandals (muṭāraqat al-naʿl), and everything with its like above it is a ṭarīqa; or because they are the paths of the angels and their comings and goings. It is also said: the celestial spheres, because they are the paths of the stars, in which their courses run. By "creation" He meant the heavens, as though He said: We created them above them "and We were never unaware of them," nor of preserving them and holding them back from falling upon them, by Our power; or He meant by it people, and that He created them above them only to open upon them provisions and blessings from them and to benefit them with the various kinds of their benefits, and He was never unaware of them and of what sets them right.
الطرائق: السموات، لأنه طورق بعضها فوق بعض كمطارقة النعل، وكل شيء فوقه مثله فهو طريقة: أو لأنها طرق الملائكة ومتقلباتهم: وقيل: الأفلاك، لأنها طرائق الكواكب فيها مسيرها: أراد بالخلق السموات، كأنه قال: خلقناها فوقهم وَما كُنَّا عنها غافِلِينَ وعن حفظها وإمساكها أن تقع فوقهم بقدرتنا: أو أراد به الناس وأنه إنما خلقها فوقهم ليفتح عليهم الأرزاق والبركات منها، وينفعهم بأنواع منافعها، وما كان غافلا عنهم وما يصلحهم.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 179
1. (1). Thus al-Thaʿlabī mentioned it from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, and al-Wāḥidī ascribed it to al-Kalbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both.
1. (1) . كذا ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وعزاه الواحدي إلى الكلبي. عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما.
12
Q 23:18 · Vol. 3, pp. 179–180

Verse 18

The verse as the commentary quotes it
"And We have sent down from the sky water in measure, and We settled it in the earth, and indeed, We are able to take it away." (18)
وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَإِنَّا عَلى ذَهابٍ بِهِ لَقادِرُونَ (18)
Vol. 3, p. 179
"In measure": by a measuring with which they are safe from harm and arrive at benefit; or by the quantity We knew of their needs and interests. "And We settled it in the earth": like His saying "and He directed it as springs in the earth." It is also said: We made it fixed in the earth. It is also said: they are five rivers: the Sayḥūn, the river of India; the Jayḥūn, the river of Balkh; the Tigris and the Euphrates, the two rivers of Iraq; and the Nile, the river of Egypt; God sent them down from a single spring among the springs of Paradise,
بِقَدَرٍ بتقدير يسلمون معه من المضرة، ويصلون إلى المنفعة. أو بمقدار ما علمناه من حاجاتهم ومصالحهم. فَأَسْكَنَّاهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ كقوله فَسَلَكَهُ يَنابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وقيل: جعلناه ثابتا في الأرض. وقيل: إنها خمسة أنهار: سيحون نهر الهند. وجيحون: نهر بلخ. ودجلة والفرات: نهرا العراق. والنيل: نهر مصر، أنزلها الله من عين واحدة من عيون الجنة،
Vol. 3, p. 180
and entrusted them to the mountains, and made them flow in the earth, and placed in them benefits for people in the various kinds of their livelihoods. And just as He was able to send it down, He is able to lift it and remove it. His saying "to take it away" is among the most telling of indefinite nouns, and the one that strikes the joint most precisely. The meaning: by one of the ways of taking it away and one of its paths. In it is a notification of the power of the one who takes it away and that nothing is beyond Him when He wills it, and it is more effective as a threat than His saying: "Say, have you considered: if your water were to become sunken, then who could bring you flowing water?" So it is for the servants to regard the favor in water as great and to bind it with constant thanks, and to fear its flight if it is not thanked.
فاستودعها الجبال، وأجراها في الأرض، وجعل فيها منافع للناس في أصناف معايشهم. وكما قدر على إنزاله فهو قادر على رفعه وإزالته. وقوله عَلى ذَهابٍ بِهِ من أوقع النكرات وأحزها للمفصل. والمعنى: على وجه من وجوه الذهاب به وطريق من طرقه. وفيه إيذان باقتدار المذهب، وأنه لا يتعايى عليه شيء إذا أراده، وهو أبلغ في الإيعاد، من قوله: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَصْبَحَ ماؤُكُمْ غَوْراً فَمَنْ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِماءٍ مَعِينٍ فعلى العباد أن يستعظموا النعمة في الماء ويقيدوها بالشكر الدائم، ويخافوا نفارها إذا لم تشكر.
Editor’s notes on these 2 pages
Vol. 3, p. 179
1. (1). Thus al-Thaʿlabī mentioned it from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both, and al-Wāḥidī ascribed it to al-Kalbī, from Ibn ʿAbbās ؓ both.
1. (1) . كذا ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما وعزاه الواحدي إلى الكلبي. عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما.
Vol. 3, p. 180
1. (1). "When the ashen year has ravaged the people, / and the noblest of men have been afflicted in the lean years by consumption; / I saw those in need around their houses, / dwelling there, until the vegetation sprouted. / There, if they are asked to grant wealth, they grant it; / if they are asked, they give; and if they play at maysir, they raise the stakes. / Among them are gatherings with fair faces, / and assemblies frequented by word and deed." By Zuhayr b. Abī Sulmā, praising Sinān b. Abī Ḥāritha. Al-shahbāʾ: the mare whose blackness is mixed with white; he likened the barren year to her because of the abundance of white in its land and its lack of the black of plants and rains, or because the light of wealth is mixed in it with the darkness of poverty. Ajḥafat bi-l-nās: that is, it carried them away and wiped from them the traces of wealth, and the attribution is a rational figure (majāz ʿaqlī). Al-jaḥra (with the jīm first, with fatḥa): the barren year; it is also related as "fī al-ḥujra." Its origin is with a vowelled [middle letter], so its sukūn is a dialectal form or by necessity, and it means severity of misery. It may also be read with ḍamma [al-ḥujra] in the sense of "house," that is: "and the eating afflicted the noble people," and their arrival [at it] was inside their houses because of their miserliness that year. It is related: "karām al-māl." The meaning is that the choicest of wealth was afflicted by consumption and diminution in that year because of the drought. "Raʾayta" is the answer to "idhā." "Dhawī al-ḥājāt": a metonymy for the poor. "Ḥawla buyūtihim": that is, of Sinān and his people. "Qaṭīnan": that is, residents; it is applied to the singular and the plural; it is also said that it is a plural. It is related as "qaṭīnan lahum": that is, living alongside them near the houses, and that is a metonymy for their generosity. "Ḥattā idhā anbata al-baql": that is, fresh vegetation sprouted and fertility appeared; "hunālika": that is, at that time, "if one asks them to bestow much wealth on him, they bestow it," that is, they give him charge over it; and if they are asked for a little wealth they give the asker. It is related: "in yastakhbilū al-māl yukhbilū," with the bāʾ: that is, one of them borrows their camels to benefit from their milk and wool in the time of drought and then returns them, they lend them to him; and if he asks them to give without return, they give him, so they do not turn away an asker. "Wa-in yaysirū": that is, they play maysir; "yughlū": that is, they make the stake high and large, for they have no fear for the poor, because wealth is plentiful, unlike the time of drought. It is also possible to read: "wa-in yusrū," that is, they are given without asking, "yaflū," with fāʾ, that is, they look after the poor and give them. One says: yasara, like waʿada: he played maysir; and yasira, like tariba and taʿiba: because wariqa [and] rafiqa. It is also related: "yasʾalū wa-yaysirū" in the imperfect. Al-maqāmāt: the gathering places of people. It is related: "wujūhuhā." In every case the pronoun refers to al-maqāmāt. Al-andiya, plural of al-nadā in the sense of generosity, irregularly; "yantābuhā": that is, their speech and their action come over them turn after turn; or the speech and action of the people circulate in them. It is possible that it is a plural of nādin, meaning a place where people converse, or of nadan on the pattern of faʿīl likewise; "yantābuhā": that is, speech and action come to it turn after turn, that is, righteous deeds.
1. (1) . إذا السنة الشهباء بالناس أجحفت
…. ونال كرام الناس في الجحرة الأكل رأيت ذوى الحاجات حول بيوتهم
…. قطينا بها حتى إذا أنبت البقل هنالك إن يستخولوا المال يخولوا
…. وإن سئلوا يعطوا وإن يسروا يغلوا وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم
…. وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل لزهير بن أبى سلمي يمدح سنان بن أبى حارثة، والشهباء: الفرس يخالط سوادها بياض، شبه بها السنة المجدبة لكثرة بياض أرضها وخلوها عن سواد النبات والأمطار. أو لاختلاط نور الغنى فيها بظلمة الفقر. أجحفت بالناس: أى ذهبت بهم ومحقت عنهم آثار الغنى، والاسناد مجاز عقلى. والجحرة- بتقديم الجيم المفتوحة-: السنة المجدبة وروى: في الحجرة. وأصلها بالتحريك، فسكونها لغة أو ضرورة وهي شدة الشقاء. ويجوز أن تقرأ بالضم بمعنى البيت، أى: ونال الأكل كرام الناس. ووصلهم داخل بيوتهم لبخلهم تلك السنة. ويروى: كرام المال. والمعنى أن كرائم الأموال نالها التأكل والتنقص في تلك السنة لجديها. ورأيت: جواب إذا. وذوى الحاجات: كناية عن الفقراء. حول بيوتهم: أى سنان وقومه. قطينا: أى مقيمين، فهو يطلق على الواحد والمتعدد. وقيل أنه جمع. ويروى قطينا لهم: أى مساكنين لهم عند البيوت، وذلك كناية عن كرمهم، حتى إذا أنبت البقل: أى نبت النبات الرطب وظهر الخصب، فهنالك: أى في ذلك الزمان إن يسألهم أحد أن يخولوه مالا كثيرا يخولوه: أى يولوه عليه. وإن سئلوا مالا قليلا يعطوا السائل. ويروى: إن يستخبلوا المال يخبلوا، بالموحدة، يستعر: أى منهم أحد إبلهم للانتفاع بألبانها وأوبارها زمن الجدب ثم يردها: أعاروه، وإن سألهم الإعطاء من غير رد أعطوه فلا يردون سائلا. وإن يسروا: أى لعبوا الميسر، يغلوا: أى يجعلوا الخطر غاليا كثيرا لعدم خوفهم على الفقراء لأن المال كثير بخلاف زمن الجدب. ويجوز أن يقرأ: وإن يسروا أى أعطوا بلا سؤال، يفلوا بالفاء. أى يتفقدوا الفقراء ويعطوهم، يقال: يسر كوعد: لعب الميسر، ويسر كترب وتعب: لأن ورق ورفق. وروى: يسألوا وييسروا بالمضارع. والمقامات: المجامع من الناس. وروى: وجوهها. وعلى كل فالضمير للمقامات. والأندية- جمع الندى- بمعنى الكرم، على غير قياس، ينتابها: أى يحرى عليها نوبة بعد نوبة قولهم وفعلهم. أو يتداولها قول الناس وفعلهم. ويحتمل أنها جمع ناد بمعنى متحدث القوم. أو ندى على فعيل كذلك، ينتابها: أى يجيئها نوبة بعد نوبة القول والفعل، أى: الصالحات.
13
Q 23:19–20 · Vol. 3, pp. 180–181

Verses 19 to 20

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And We brought forth for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines, in which for you are abundant fruits and from which you eat," (19) "and [We brought forth] a tree issuing from Mount Sinai, which grows [producing] oil and a condiment for those who eat." (20)
فَأَنْشَأْنا لَكُمْ بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنابٍ لَكُمْ فِيها فَواكِهُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ (19) وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ طُورِ سَيْناءَ تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ وَصِبْغٍ لِلْآكِلِينَ (20)
Vol. 3, p. 180
He singled out these three kinds because they are the noblest and most excellent of trees and the most comprehensive in benefits. He described the palm and the vine as having fruit that combines two things: that it is a fruit one enjoys, and a food that is eaten fresh and dry, fresh and as grapes, and as dates and raisins. And the olive in that its oil is suitable both for lamps and for dipping. It is possible that His saying "and from them you eat" comes from their saying: "so-and-so eats from a trade he practices, from an estate whose yield he collects, from a business by which he profits," meaning that it is his source of food and the direction from which his provision comes, as though He said: these gardens are the sources of your provisions and your livelihoods, from which you are provided for and live. "And a tree": a conjunction upon "gardens." It has also been read in the nominative, as a subject: that is, "and among what has been brought forth for you is a tree." "Ṭūr Saynāʾ" and "Ṭūr Sīnīn": it must be either that al-Ṭūr is annexed to a place named Saynāʾ and Sīnūn, or that it is a name for the mountain composed of an annexed term and an annexed-to term, like Imruʾ al-Qays and like Baʿlabakk, for those who annex it. Whoever reads Sīnāʾ with kasra on the sīn has made it diptote because of definiteness and foreign origin or femininity, since it is a place, and the pattern fiʿlāʾ does not have an alif of femininity, like ʿilbāʾ and ḥirbāʾ. And whoever reads it with fatḥa did not make it a triptote, because the alif is for femininity, like ṣaḥrāʾ. It is also said: it is a mountain of Palestine. It is also said: between Egypt and Ayla. From it Moses ﷺ was called. Al-Aʿmash read: Sīnā, shortened. "With oil" is in the position of a circumstantial clause, that is: it grows with the oil in it. It has also been read: tunbit. There are two ways [of explaining] it: the first, that anbata has the sense of nabata. And he recited from Zuhayr: "I saw those in need around their houses, dwelling there, until the vegetation sprouted (1)."
خصّ هذه الأنواع الثلاثة، لأنها أكرم الشجر وأفضلها وأجمعها للمنافع. ووصف النخل والعنب بأنّ ثمرهما جامع بين أمرين: بأنه فاكهة يتفكه بها، وطعام يؤكل رطبا ويابسا، رطبا وعنبا، وتمرا وزبيبا. والزيتون بأنّ دهنه صالح للاستصباح والاصطباغ جميعا. ويجوز أن يكون قوله وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ من قولهم: يأكل فلان من حرفة يحترفها، ومن ضيعة يغتلها، ومن تجارة يتربح بها: يعنون أنها طعمته وجهته التي منها يحصل رزقه، كأنه قال: وهذه الجنات وجوه أرزاقكم ومعايشكم، منها ترتزقون وتتعيشون وَشَجَرَةً عطف على جنات. وقرئت مرفوعة على الابتداء، أى: ومما أنشئ لكم شجرة طُورِ سَيْناءَ وطور سينين، لا يخلو إما أن يضاف فيه الطور إلى بقعة اسمها سيناء وسينون، وإمّا أن يكون اسما للجبل مركبا من مضاف ومضاف إليه، كإمرئ القيس، وكبعلبك، فيمن أضاف. فمن كسر سين سيناء فقد منع الصرف للتعريف والعجمة أو التأنيث، لأنها بقعة، وفعلاء لا يكون ألفه للتأنيث كعلباء وحرباء. ومن فتح فلم يصرف، لأنّ الألف للتأنيث كصحراء. وقيل: هو جبل فلسطين. وقيل: بين مصر وأيلة. ومنه نودي موسى عليه السلام. وقرأ الأعمش: سينا على القصر بِالدُّهْنِ في موضع الحال، أى: تنبت وفيها الدهن. وقرئ: تنبت. وفيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن أنبت بمعنى نبت. وأنشد لزهير: رأيت ذوى الحاجات حول بيوتهم … قطينا لهم حتّي إذا أنبت البقل «1»
Vol. 3, p. 181
and the second, that its object is omitted, that is: it grows its olives, and in it is the oil. It has also been read: tunbatu, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the bāʾ, and its ruling is the ruling of tunbit. Ibn Masʿūd read: takhruju al-duhna wa-ṣibghin li-l-ākilīn. Others read: takhruju bi-l-duhn; and in the codex of Ubayy: tuthmiru bi-l-duhn. On the authority of one of them: tunbitu bi-l-dihān. Al-Aʿmash read: wa-ṣibghan; and it has been read: wa-ṣibāgh. Similar are dibgh and dibāgh. Al-ṣibgh: dipping [bread] for use as a condiment. It is said: it is the first tree to grow after the Flood, and God, Exalted, described it as blessed in His saying "lit from a blessed tree."
والثاني: أنّ مفعوله محذوف، أى: تنبت زيتونها وفيه الزيت. وقرئ: تنبت، بضم التاء وفتح الباء، وحكمه حكم تنبت. وقرأ ابن مسعود: تخرج الدهن وصبغ الآكلين. وغيره: تخرج بالدهن: وفي حرف أبىّ: تثمر بالدهن. وعن بعضهم: تنبت بالدهان. وقرأ الأعمش: وصبغا وقرئ وصباغ. ونحوهما: دبغ ودباغ. والصبغ: الغمس للائتدام. وقيل: هي أوّل شجرة نبتت بعد الطوفان، ووصفها الله تعالى بالبركة في قوله يُوقَدُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 180
1. (1). "When the ashen year has ravaged the people, / and the noblest of men have been afflicted in the lean years by consumption; / I saw those in need around their houses, / dwelling there, until the vegetation sprouted. / There, if they are asked to grant wealth, they grant it; / if they are asked, they give; and if they play at maysir, they raise the stakes. / Among them are gatherings with fair faces, / and assemblies frequented by word and deed." By Zuhayr b. Abī Sulmā, praising Sinān b. Abī Ḥāritha. Al-shahbāʾ: the mare whose blackness is mixed with white; he likened the barren year to her because of the abundance of white in its land and its lack of the black of plants and rains, or because the light of wealth is mixed in it with the darkness of poverty. Ajḥafat bi-l-nās: that is, it carried them away and wiped from them the traces of wealth, and the attribution is a rational figure (majāz ʿaqlī). Al-jaḥra (with the jīm first, with fatḥa): the barren year; it is also related as "fī al-ḥujra." Its origin is with a vowelled [middle letter], so its sukūn is a dialectal form or by necessity, and it means severity of misery. It may also be read with ḍamma [al-ḥujra] in the sense of "house," that is: "and the eating afflicted the noble people," and their arrival [at it] was inside their houses because of their miserliness that year. It is related: "karām al-māl." The meaning is that the choicest of wealth was afflicted by consumption and diminution in that year because of the drought. "Raʾayta" is the answer to "idhā." "Dhawī al-ḥājāt": a metonymy for the poor. "Ḥawla buyūtihim": that is, of Sinān and his people. "Qaṭīnan": that is, residents; it is applied to the singular and the plural; it is also said that it is a plural. It is related as "qaṭīnan lahum": that is, living alongside them near the houses, and that is a metonymy for their generosity. "Ḥattā idhā anbata al-baql": that is, fresh vegetation sprouted and fertility appeared; "hunālika": that is, at that time, "if one asks them to bestow much wealth on him, they bestow it," that is, they give him charge over it; and if they are asked for a little wealth they give the asker. It is related: "in yastakhbilū al-māl yukhbilū," with the bāʾ: that is, one of them borrows their camels to benefit from their milk and wool in the time of drought and then returns them, they lend them to him; and if he asks them to give without return, they give him, so they do not turn away an asker. "Wa-in yaysirū": that is, they play maysir; "yughlū": that is, they make the stake high and large, for they have no fear for the poor, because wealth is plentiful, unlike the time of drought. It is also possible to read: "wa-in yusrū," that is, they are given without asking, "yaflū," with fāʾ, that is, they look after the poor and give them. One says: yasara, like waʿada: he played maysir; and yasira, like tariba and taʿiba: because wariqa [and] rafiqa. It is also related: "yasʾalū wa-yaysirū" in the imperfect. Al-maqāmāt: the gathering places of people. It is related: "wujūhuhā." In every case the pronoun refers to al-maqāmāt. Al-andiya, plural of al-nadā in the sense of generosity, irregularly; "yantābuhā": that is, their speech and their action come over them turn after turn; or the speech and action of the people circulate in them. It is possible that it is a plural of nādin, meaning a place where people converse, or of nadan on the pattern of faʿīl likewise; "yantābuhā": that is, speech and action come to it turn after turn, that is, righteous deeds.
1. (1) . إذا السنة الشهباء بالناس أجحفت

Q 23:21–22 · Vol. 3, pp. 181–182

Verses 21 to 22

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And indeed, for you in the livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from that which is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat." (21) "And upon them and upon ships you are carried." (22)
وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِها وَلَكُمْ فِيها مَنافِعُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ (21) وَعَلَيْها وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ (22)
Vol. 3, p. 181
It has been read: tusqīkum, with a tāʾ with fatḥa, that is: the livestock give you drink. "And from them you eat": that is, benefits attach to them, of riding, carrying and other things, as they attach to animals whose flesh is not eaten, such as horses, mules and donkeys; and in them is an additional benefit, which is eating, a benefit from their very selves. The livestock are meant by the camels, because they are what is customarily carried upon, and He paired them with ships, that is, boats, because they are the boats of the land. Dhū al-Rumma said:
قرئ: تسقيكم، بتاء مفتوحة، أى: تسقيكم الأنعام وَمِنْها تَأْكُلُونَ أى تتعلق بها منافع من الركوب والحمل وغير ذلك، كما تتعلق بما لا يؤكل لحمه من الخيل والبغال والحمير. وفيها منفعة زائدة، وهي الأكل الذي هو انتفاع بذواتها، والقصد بالأنعام إلى الإبل لأنها هي المحمول عليها في العادة، وقرنها بالفلك- التي هي السفائن- لأنها سفائن البرّ. قال ذو الرمة:
Vol. 3, p. 182
"A ship of the land, its halter beneath my cheeks (1)," meaning his she-camel Ṣaydaḥ (2).
سفينة برّ تحت خدّى زمامها «1» يريد صيدحه «2»
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 182
1. (1). "Hark! Mayy appeared in a vision while my companions slept, / and nothing drove off the drowsing but her greeting, / coming by night; and the frame of the saddle was bound upon / a ship of the land, its halter beneath my cheeks. / She was made to kneel and laid down one hard patch upon another, / with few sounds there except her bellowing." By Dhū al-Rumma. He says: khayyalat Mayyun, that is: she sent her phantom and showed it to me, and greeted me in my sleep, while my companions had slept, al-ṣuḥba being like al-ʿuṣba and al-rufqa; and he ascribed sleep to them and not to himself because his sleep was tahwīm, that is, languor and heedlessness only at the beginning of sleep; al-tahwīm is also the nodding of the head from drowsiness; or [he ascribed it to them] because he was remembering her, so it was as though he had not slept. It is related: "dhū al-karā" in place of "ṣaḥbī": "nothing drove off the drowsing and dismissed it from me but her greeting upon me." It is related: "Alā ṭaraqatnā Mayyatu bintu Mundhirin / fa-mā arraqa al-niyāma illā salāmuhā": arraqa: kept awake; al-niyām: plural of nāʾim, whose analogical form would be nuwwām, but the wāw was turned into yāʾ irregularly. Al-ṭurūq: coming at night, and it is accusative as a verbal noun of khayyalat, because they coincide in meaning. It is also said: al-ṭarūq (with fatḥa) is the she-camel old enough to be covered by the stallion, and it is the object of khayyalat. The more apt view is that it is a circumstantial clause qualifying its subject here, and perhaps it is by way of comparison. Jalb al-raḥl (with ḍamma, and with kasra): its wooden pieces, that is: the circumstance being that the pieces of the saddle are bound upon a great she-camel like a ship. So he borrowed [the word] "ship" for her by way of explicit metaphor, and its annexation to the land is the clue to the metaphor. In it is that on land she takes the place of the ship on the sea and corresponds to it, and the halter is a stripping [of the metaphor] (tajrīd), that is: her halter was under my cheeks while I was asleep. Al-balda of the she-camel: that which touches the ground when she kneels, and it is applied to the chest. Al-balda is also hard ground. Al-bughām: the cry of the gazelle, that is: I made her kneel and she laid down hard bones like the ground, so he borrowed [the word] for her by way of explicit metaphor, upon hard ground, the circumstance being that this ground has few sounds in it except the bughām of the she-camel, that is, her voice resembling the voice of the gazelle, because it was a moaning. The coming of a circumstantial clause from an indefinite noun with no postposing, negation or specification is irregular. It is related: qalīlin, in the genitive, as a description. In either case al-aṣwāt is its subject, and the nominative of the excepted element is by following, because qalīl is in the sense of negation, that is: there is in it no sound except the bughām. It is also said that "illā" here means "ghayr," so it is a description of the sounds, because it resembles an indefinite noun, and when the appearance of the case ending on it became impossible, it appeared on what follows it.
2. . His statement "yurīdu Ṣaydaḥahu": that is, his she-camel called Ṣaydaḥ. (ʿ)
1. (1) . ألا خيلت مى وقد نام صحبتي
…. فما نفر التهويم إلا سلامها طروقا وجلب الرحل مشدودة به
…. سفينة بر تحت خدي زمامها أنيخت فألقت بلدة فوق بلدة
…. قليلا بها الأصوات إلا بغامها لذي الرمة، يقول: خيلت مى، أى: بعثت خيالها وأرتنى إياه، وسلمت على في منامي. والحال أنه قد نام أصحابى، والصحبة كالعصبة والرفقة، ونسب النوم إليهم دونه، لأن نومه تهويم أى فتور وغفلة أول النوم فقط. والتهويم أيضا: تمايل الرأس من النعاس، أو لأنه يتذكرها فكأنه لم ينم. ويروى: ذو الكرى بدل صحبتي، فما نفر التهويم وطرده عنى إلا سلامها على. ويروى: ألا طرقتنا مية بنت منذر
…. فما أرّق النيام إلا سلامها وأرق: أسهر، والنيام: جمع نائم، وقياسه نوام، فقلب ياء شذوذا، والطروق: الإتيان ليلا، وهو نصب على المصدر من خيلت، لتلاقيهما معنى. وقيل: الطروق- بالفتح-: الناقة التي بلغت أن يطرقها الفحل، وهو مفعول خيلت. والأوجه أنه حال من فاعله هذا، ولعله على التشبيه. وجلب الرحل- بالضم، وبالكسر-: عيدانه، أى: والحال أن عيدان الرحل مشدودة بها ناقة عظيمة كالسفينة. فاستعارها لها على طريق التصريح، وإضافتها للبر قرينة للاستعارة. وفيه أنها في البر تقوم مقام السفينة في البحر، وأنها تقابلها، والزمام تجريد، أى: زمامها تحت خدي وأنا نائم. والبلدة من الناقة: ما لاقى الأرض عند الاناخة، وتطلق على الصدر. والبلدة الأرض الصلبة. والبغام: صوت الظبى، أى: أنختها فألقت عظاما صلبة كالأرض، فاستعارها لها على طريق التصريح، فوق أرض صلبة حال كون تلك الأرض قليلا فيها الأصوات إلا نعام الناقة، أى: صوتها الشبيه بصوت الظبى، لأنه كان حنينا. ومجيء الحال من النكرة بلا تأخير ولا نفى ولا تخصيص شاذ. ويروى. قليل- بالجر- على الصفة. وعلى كل فالأصوات فاعل له، ورفع المستثنى على الاتباع، لأن قليلا في معنى النفي، أى: ليس فيها صوت إلا البغام. وقيل «إلا» هنا بمعنى غير، فهي صفة للأصوات لأنه يشبه النكرة، ولما تعذر ظهور الاعراب عليها ظهر على ما بعدها.
2. . قوله «يريد صيدحه» أى: ناقته المسماة بصيدح. (ع)
15
Q 23:23–25 · Vol. 3, pp. 182–183

Verses 23 to 25

The verses as the commentary quotes them
"And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?'" (23) "But the eminent among those who disbelieved from his people said, 'This is not but a man like yourselves who wishes to take precedence over you; and if God had willed [to send a messenger], He would have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers.'" (24) "'He is not but a man possessed with madness, so wait concerning him for a time.'" (25)
وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَقالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ (23) فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ ما هذا إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَأَنْزَلَ مَلائِكَةً ما سَمِعْنا بِهذا فِي آبائِنَا الْأَوَّلِينَ (24) إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ رَجُلٌ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ فَتَرَبَّصُوا بِهِ حَتَّى حِينٍ (25)
Vol. 3, p. 182
"Ghayruhu" is in the nominative by locus and in the genitive by wording, and the sentence is a new beginning that functions as a reason for the command to worship. "Then will you not fear Him": will you not fear that you will abandon worship of God, who is your Lord and Creator and Provider, when thanks for His favor, which you cannot count, is obligatory upon you, and then go and worship other than Him, which has no claim to
غَيْرُهُ بالرفع على المحل، وبالجرّ على اللفظ، والجملة استئناف تجرى مجرى التعليل للأمر بالعبادة أَفَلا تَتَّقُونَ أفلا تخافون أن ترفضوا عبادة الله الذي هو ربكم وخالقكم ورازقكم، وشكر نعمته التي لا تحصونها واجب عليكم، ثم تذهبوا فتعبدوا غيره مما ليس من استحقاق
Vol. 3, p. 183
worship in any respect. "To take precedence over you": to seek superiority over you and be your chief, like His saying "and that you two may have greatness in the land." "Of this" is a reference to Noah ﷺ or to what he addressed them with of urging worship of God, that is: we have not heard the like of this speech, or the like of this one who claims, while being a man, that he is the Messenger of God. How astonishing is the case of error! They were not pleased with a man for prophethood, yet they were pleased with a stone for divinity. Their saying "we have not heard of this" indicates that they and their forefathers lived in a long interval [between prophets]; or they lied in that, because of their absorption in error and their readiness to repel the truth by whatever means they could and whatever occurred to them, without distinguishing between truth and falsehood. Do you not see how they called him mad, when they knew that he was the soundest of people in intellect and the weightiest in speech? Al-jinna: madness or jinn, that is: he has jinn who derange him. "For a time": that is, bear with him and be patient with him for a period, until his affair is cleared up in an outcome; if he recovers from his madness, [well], and if not, you will kill him.
العبادة في شيء أَنْ يَتَفَضَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ أن يطلب الفضل عليكم ويرأسكم، كقوله تعالى وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي الْأَرْضِ. بِهذا إشارة إلى نوح عليه السلام، أو إلى ما كلهم به من الحث على عبادة الله، أى: ما سمعنا بمثل هذا الكلام، أو بمثل هذا الذي يدعى وهو بشر أنه رسول الله، وما أعجب شأن الضلال لم يرضوا للنبوّة ببشر وقد رضوا للإلهية بحجر: وقولهم ما سَمِعْنا بِهذا يدل على أنهم وآباؤهم كانوا في فترة متطاولة. أو تكذبوا في ذلك لانهماكهم في الغى، وتشمرهم لأن يدفعوا الحق بما أمكنهم وبما عنّ لهم، من غير تمييز منهم بين صدق وكذب. ألا تراهم: كيف جننوه وقد علموا أنه أرجح الناس عقلا وأوزنهم قولا. والجنة: الجنون أو الجنّ، أى: به جنّ يخبلونه حَتَّى حِينٍ أى احتملوه واصبروا عليه إلى زمان، حتى ينجلي أمره عن عاقبة، فإن أفاق من جنونه وإلا قتلتموه.
Editor’s notes on this page
Vol. 3, p. 182
1. (1). "Hark! Mayy appeared in a vision while my companions slept, / and nothing drove off the drowsing but her greeting, / coming by night; and the frame of the saddle was bound upon / a ship of the land, its halter beneath my cheeks. / She was made to kneel and laid down one hard patch upon another, / with few sounds there except her bellowing." By Dhū al-Rumma. He says: khayyalat Mayyun, that is: she sent her phantom and showed it to me, and greeted me in my sleep, while my companions had slept, al-ṣuḥba being like al-ʿuṣba and al-rufqa; and he ascribed sleep to them and not to himself because his sleep was tahwīm, that is, languor and heedlessness only at the beginning of sleep; al-tahwīm is also the nodding of the head from drowsiness; or [he ascribed it to them] because he was remembering her, so it was as though he had not slept. It is related: "dhū al-karā" in place of "ṣaḥbī": "nothing drove off the drowsing and dismissed it from me but her greeting upon me." It is related: "Alā ṭaraqatnā Mayyatu bintu Mundhirin / fa-mā arraqa al-niyāma illā salāmuhā": arraqa: kept awake; al-niyām: plural of nāʾim, whose analogical form would be nuwwām, but the wāw was turned into yāʾ irregularly. Al-ṭurūq: coming at night, and it is accusative as a verbal noun of khayyalat, because they coincide in meaning. It is also said: al-ṭarūq (with fatḥa) is the she-camel old enough to be covered by the stallion, and it is the object of khayyalat. The more apt view is that it is a circumstantial clause qualifying its subject here, and perhaps it is by way of comparison. Jalb al-raḥl (with ḍamma, and with kasra): its wooden pieces, that is: the circumstance being that the pieces of the saddle are bound upon a great she-camel like a ship. So he borrowed [the word] "ship" for her by way of explicit metaphor, and its annexation to the land is the clue to the metaphor. In it is that on land she takes the place of the ship on the sea and corresponds to it, and the halter is a stripping [of the metaphor] (tajrīd), that is: her halter was under my cheeks while I was asleep. Al-balda of the she-camel: that which touches the ground when she kneels, and it is applied to the chest. Al-balda is also hard ground. Al-bughām: the cry of the gazelle, that is: I made her kneel and she laid down hard bones like the ground, so he borrowed [the word] for her by way of explicit metaphor, upon hard ground, the circumstance being that this ground has few sounds in it except the bughām of the she-camel, that is, her voice resembling the voice of the gazelle, because it was a moaning. The coming of a circumstantial clause from an indefinite noun with no postposing, negation or specification is irregular. It is related: qalīlin, in the genitive, as a description. In either case al-aṣwāt is its subject, and the nominative of the excepted element is by following, because qalīl is in the sense of negation, that is: there is in it no sound except the bughām. It is also said that "illā" here means "ghayr," so it is a description of the sounds, because it resembles an indefinite noun, and when the appearance of the case ending on it became impossible, it appeared on what follows it.
2. . His statement "yurīdu Ṣaydaḥahu": that is, his she-camel called Ṣaydaḥ. (ʿ)
1. (1) . ألا خيلت مى وقد نام صحبتي
…. فما نفر التهويم إلا سلامها طروقا وجلب الرحل مشدودة به
…. سفينة بر تحت خدي زمامها أنيخت فألقت بلدة فوق بلدة
…. قليلا بها الأصوات إلا بغامها لذي الرمة، يقول: خيلت مى، أى: بعثت خيالها وأرتنى إياه، وسلمت على في منامي. والحال أنه قد نام أصحابى، والصحبة كالعصبة والرفقة، ونسب النوم إليهم دونه، لأن نومه تهويم أى فتور وغفلة أول النوم فقط. والتهويم أيضا: تمايل الرأس من النعاس، أو لأنه يتذكرها فكأنه لم ينم. ويروى: ذو الكرى بدل صحبتي، فما نفر التهويم وطرده عنى إلا سلامها على. ويروى: ألا طرقتنا مية بنت منذر
